meta.document: AI Trucking Back-Office Platform — Master Build Prompt
meta.how_to_use: Give this whole file to the coding agent (e.g. Claude Code) as the project brief. Sections marked TEMPORARY DEFAULT may be changed by the founder; everything else is a requirement.
changes_from_v1: Added market context, target customer, business model and pilot plan from the November 2026 research brief.
Added a done-for-you service model: AI does the work, an internal reviewer confirms flags, the owner approves.
Added zero-typing intake: phone photos, email forwarding, WhatsApp/SMS, fuel card CSV import and ELD mileage import.
Replaced 'AI checks itself' with deterministic rule checks plus a second independent extraction pass.
Added a full validation rule catalog with codes, severities and deterministic checks.
Added a full relational data model, field-level provenance and edit history.
Added IFTA calculation logic, rate-table handling and 4-year record retention.
Added receipt-to-fuel-card matching, report and CSV specs, i18n (English and Somali), metrics, cost controls, test fixtures and a dated roadmap with gates.
Added a recommended stack as a TEMPORARY DEFAULT, with trade-offs.

role: You are a senior product architect, AI engineer, full-stack developer, and practical startup partner. Build a real, secure, production-minded AI back-office platform for trucking companies. Be honest about what is implemented, prioritize accuracy and traceability, and never pretend unfinished features work. Act as the technical co-founder: make sensible decisions autonomously, label assumptions, and only stop to ask the founder when a choice is expensive to reverse, involves money or legal exposure, or contradicts this brief.

project.mission: Help trucking companies run their back office by turning documents into organized, verified, actionable business records.
project.company_ownership: The software is owned by the founder's venture, not by A&H FREIGHT GROUP LLC. A&H is the first pilot customer and design partner. Put a short written data-use agreement in place before processing their real documents.
project.budget: Undecided; prototype first and avoid unnecessary costs.
project.product_strategy: Architect for a larger platform but build one complete, testable module at a time.
languages: Somali (owner-facing UI, notifications and report summaries)
project.one_line_promise: Send us your paperwork. Every month you get clean books and IFTA-ready numbers, checked by AI and confirmed by a person, with every number traceable to its receipt.

key_dates.first_customer_deadline: 2027-02-01 — Q4 2026 IFTA returns due. The pilot must deliver a complete, preparer-ready Q4 2026 IFTA package for A&H before this date.

market_context.summary: Very small carriers dominate U.S. trucking, pay several separate vendors for back-office help, and still do the paperwork by hand.

facts.fact: Fleets of 1–6 tractors are about 86% of U.S. carriers; fleets of 7–19 are another 9%.
About 88,000 carrier authorities were lost between January 2025 and February 2026; surviving carriers are cost-sensitive.
IFTA records must be kept 4 years from the return due date or filing date, whichever is later; burden of proof is on the carrier.
Fuel receipts missing required details can be disallowed as tax-paid credits in an audit.
Software: Rigbooks $19–$149/mo; TruckingOffice $25–$90/mo; TruckLogics $39.95–$249.95/mo plus ~$20–$25 per IFTA report.
Factoring costs small carriers roughly 2–5% of invoice value.
Funded AI-native players (Datatruck $12M Series A, Bubba, Transflo Workflow AI) target growing and mid-size fleets willing to replace their whole system.

market_context.our_gap: Priced like software, delivered like a service; plugs into what the owner already uses; audit-proof by design; Somali-language support for our first community.

target_customer.primary: U.S. for-hire carriers with 1–10 power units running interstate (IFTA-licensed), where the owner does the back office personally.
target_customer.first_50_customers: Somali and East African owner-operators and small fleets reached through the founder's network, community groups and referrals.
target_customer.secondary_buyer: Trucking bookkeepers and IFTA/permit service firms who manage many carriers and need clean, traceable paperwork (partner role, multi-company access).
target_customer.not_now: Mid-size and enterprise fleets, brokers, intrastate-only carriers, Canadian-based carriers.

business_model.pricing_rule: Do not hard-code prices. Store plans in configuration. Billing integration (e.g. Stripe) is out of scope until the pilot validates willingness to pay.
business_model.later_revenue: Referral partnerships with factoring companies and fuel card providers once we hold verified invoices and fuel data (year two decision; requires explicit customer consent).

product_vision.core_differentiator: An AI agent that processes trucking paperwork end to end, checks its results against source documents, explains discrepancies, keeps evidence linked to every record, and prepares professional reports for human review.
product_vision.guiding_promise: The owner never types data. They send documents, approve results, and download deliverables.
product_vision.competitive_stance: Do not try to replace the ELD, fuel card, dispatch or factoring provider. Ingest their outputs and become the verified record that sits on top of them.

service_model.description: Hybrid AI + human service. AI extracts and checks everything; an internal reviewer resolves flagged items within an SLA; the owner approves anything consequential.

roles.can: See everything for their company, approve corrections, approve and download reports, manage users, vehicles and drivers.
Upload, review and correct; cannot approve final reports unless granted.
Submit documents via phone camera, WhatsApp, SMS or email; see only their own submissions and statuses.
Work the cross-company review queue for assigned companies; resolve flags; every action logged; cannot export or delete customer data.
Access multiple client companies they are invited to; same rights as office staff per company.
Manage tenants, plans, rate tables and system config; access customer documents only through a logged break-glass action.

service_model.review_sla_TEMPORARY_DEFAULT: Flagged items resolved within 1 business day; quarter-end packages within 2 business days of the last document.
reviewer_console: Queue across assigned companies, sorted by deadline and severity.
Side-by-side source image (zoomable, with highlighted field region) and extracted fields from both passes.
One-click accept pass A / accept pass B / enter value / mark unreadable / request info from customer.
Requests to the customer go out as a message in their chosen channel and language.
Track reviewer minutes per document as a cost metric.

intake_channels.principle: Meet owners and drivers where they already are. Every channel lands in the same documents pipeline with identical processing.

channels.details: Drag-and-drop multi-file upload; PDF, JPG, PNG, HEIC, TIFF, CSV, XLSX; per-file progress and errors.
Installable PWA on iPhone/Android; multi-shot capture, auto-crop, blur and glare warnings before upload; offline queue that uploads when signal returns.
Each company gets a unique inbound address (e.g. docs+<company-slug>@<domain>). Attachments become documents; sender must be a registered user or is held for owner approval.

Twilio (or equivalent) number. Sender phone maps to a user/driver and company. Photos become documents; the bot replies with a receipt confirmation and asks only for missing essentials (e.g. truck unit number) in the user's language. Unknown senders are rejected politely.
CSV/XLSX import with saved column mappings per provider (Comdata, WEX/EFS, AtoB, TCS, generic). Each row becomes a fuel_card_transaction, not a duplicate receipt.
Import the ELD's IFTA/jurisdiction mileage report (CSV/XLSX/PDF) per vehicle and quarter. Direct API integrations (Motive, Samsara, etc.) are phase 3.
CSV/OFX import for expense matching and bookkeeping.

attribution_rules: Every document gets company, reporting period (derived from transaction date, overridable), uploader and channel.
Truck unit number is captured from the receipt, the fuel card row, the driver's default truck, or by asking — in that order, recording which source was used.
Never assign a document to a company based on guesswork; unattributable documents go to an 'Unassigned' inbox.

mvp.name: Document Processing and Audit Center (with IFTA-ready output)
mvp.goal: A trucking owner can upload a batch of receipts and receive an organized transaction ledger, state-by-state fuel summary when supported, an exception list, and a professional downloadable report with source documents. For IFTA, combine verified fuel purchases with imported jurisdiction mileage to produce a preparer-ready quarterly worksheet, clearly labeled preliminary until reviewed.
in_scope: ELD mileage import and jurisdiction summaries
Review queue (owner + internal reviewer) with edit history
PDF report, CSV export, supporting-document package, IFTA worksheet
Audit log, 4-year retention, English and Somali UI
out_of_scope_for_mvp: Filing any return with any jurisdiction
Invoicing, settlements, maintenance, full bookkeeping (later phases)
input_types: Multi-receipt photos (several receipts in one image)

workflow.name: Intake
requirements: Allow multiple documents per batch.
Associate uploads with a company and reporting period.
Show progress, failures, and processing status.
Preserve the original files unchanged.
Accept documents from every phase-1 channel into one pipeline.
Compute a SHA-256 hash of every original file; identical hashes are flagged as exact duplicates (D001) but still stored and linked.
Store originals immutably in object storage; all processing works on derived copies.

workflow.name: Pre-process
requirements: Split multi-page PDFs into pages; detect multiple receipts in one image and create one region per receipt.
Run an image quality check (blur, glare, crop, resolution) and record a quality score; poor images trigger a re-capture request rather than a guess.
Rotate and deskew derived copies only.

workflow.name: Extract — two independent passes
requirements: Extract merchant, transaction date, location, state, fuel type, gallons, unit price, fuel subtotal, taxes, fees, parking, other charges, credits, currency, and receipt total when present.
Record source filename and page or region reference where possible.
Store original extracted text/value separately from normalized values.
Use null for missing or unreadable values; never invent them.
Track confidence per field and flag low-confidence fields for review.
Pass A: vision-capable LLM reads the image and returns JSON matching the extraction contract.
Pass B: an independent read using a different prompt and either a different model or an OCR-text-then-parse path. Pass B must not see Pass A's output.
For every field store: raw text as printed, normalized value, confidence, bounding box/page reference, pass id, model id and prompt version.
Fields where passes agree (after normalization) are 'corroborated'; fields that disagree raise V010 and go to review.
Also extract when present: truck/unit number, odometer, driver name, card last 4, payment method, pump number, reefer fuel and DEF lines, purchaser name, seller address.

workflow.name: Normalize and classify
requirements: Normalize dates, state abbreviations, currency, and measurement units.
Classify fuel charges separately from non-fuel charges, taxes, fees, parking, credits, and refunds when evidence supports it.
Keep source values available for comparison.
Do not assume receipt total equals fuel spend.
Split a receipt into line items: motor fuel (diesel, gasoline), reefer fuel, DEF, other non-fuel, taxes, fees, discounts/credits.
Treat reefer fuel and DEF as separate fuel types; never add them to IFTA motor-fuel gallons. Flag for preparer confirmation.
Resolve state from the printed address; if only a city or station number is present, use a station directory lookup and mark the source as 'lookup'.

workflow.name: Validate
requirements: Flag likely duplicate documents and explain the matching evidence.
Check arithmetic when line items and totals are available.
Flag missing, conflicting, unreadable, or suspicious values.
Check date, state, unit, and total consistency where possible.
Link every issue to the relevant source document and field.
Do not silently delete, merge, or overwrite records.
Run every rule in validation_rule_catalog; rules are deterministic code, versioned, and each produces an issue with code, severity, evidence and the fields involved.

Status logic: any error-severity issue → Needs Attention; unreadable or unresolvable after review → Unable to Verify; all required fields corroborated or human-confirmed and no open errors → Verified.

workflow.name: Match and reconcile
requirements: Calculate supported totals by state and reporting period.
Separate gallons, fuel amounts, non-fuel charges, taxes, fees, credits, and overall receipt totals.
Show calculation formulas, included records, excluded records, and unresolved differences.
Preserve edit history when users correct values.
Label results preliminary until required information is reviewed and complete.
Match receipts to fuel card rows by date (±1 day), gallons (±0.5%), amount (±$0.50) and state/location; record match score and the fields used.
Matched pairs become one fuel purchase with two pieces of evidence (corroboration).
Unmatched card rows → I003 'card purchase with no receipt'. Unmatched receipts paid by card → I004.
Import ELD jurisdiction miles per vehicle; reconcile total miles against odometer readings where available (M001–M004).

workflow.name: Human review
requirements: Use statuses Verified, Needs Attention, and Unable to Verify.
Provide a review queue for uncertain fields and exceptions.
Allow users to open the source document from each transaction.
Require explicit approval for material corrections and consequential actions.
Two-tier review: internal reviewer resolves extraction flags; owner approves material corrections and final reports.
Every correction stores old value, new value, who, when, why and evidence; original extracted values are never overwritten.

workflow.name: Deliver
requirements: Generate a professional PDF summary.
Include company, reporting period, totals, state-by-state gallons where supported, exceptions, and reconciliation notes.
Allow original receipts to be appended or included as a supporting-document package.
Show report generation date and preliminary/reviewed status.
Provide CSV export for structured records.
Produce: period PDF report, transactions CSV, supporting-document package (ZIP with index), IFTA quarterly worksheet (PDF + CSV).
Every deliverable records the data snapshot it was built from, so it can be regenerated identically.
Notify the owner when a deliverable is ready, in their language and channel.

rules: Return only JSON matching the schema; no prose.
Use null for anything not clearly printed. Never infer, estimate, or compute a value the receipt does not show.
Copy raw text exactly as printed in a raw_text field alongside each normalized value.
Report a bounding box or region description for each field when possible.
List every line item separately; do not sum lines yourself.
If more than one receipt is visible, return an array with one object per receipt.
Set legibility per field: clear | partial | unreadable.
extraction_contract.model_config: Model IDs and prompt versions come from environment/config (e.g. EXTRACTION_MODEL_A, EXTRACTION_MODEL_B). Verify every model ID against the provider's current documentation before use; never hard-code a guessed model name.
extraction_contract.confidence_note: Model-reported confidence is a hint, not proof. Status depends on corroboration and rule checks, not on confidence alone.

structured_transaction_schema.ifta_taxable_gallons: number|null (motor fuel only, computed by code)
structured_transaction_schema.field_provenance: map of field → {raw_text, pass_a_value, pass_b_value, final_value, final_source: pass_a|pass_b|human|card|lookup, confidence, bbox}

validation_rule_catalog.principle: Every rule is deterministic code with a unit test. LLMs may suggest; only rules and humans decide status.

rules.check: Required IFTA receipt fields present: date, seller name, seller address/state, gallons, fuel type, amount or price per gallon.
Truck unit number present on the receipt or attributed from another recorded source (receipts lacking it may be challenged in an audit).
Purchaser/company name present on the receipt.
Transaction date is valid and within the selected reporting period (or flagged as belonging to another period).
State is a valid IFTA jurisdiction code.
Field legibility is 'partial' or 'unreadable'.
Image quality score below threshold.
Pass A and Pass B disagree on a material field (date, state, gallons, amounts, fuel type).
gallons × unit_price ≈ fuel line amount (tolerance $0.02 or 0.1%).
Sum of line items + taxes + fees − discounts ≈ receipt_total (tolerance $0.02).
Diesel unit price outside the plausible range set in config for that date.
Gallons in a single purchase exceed vehicle tank capacity (from vehicle profile) or 300 gal default.
Reefer fuel or DEF present; excluded from IFTA motor-fuel gallons pending preparer confirmation.
Units are liters or currency is not USD; converted with the factor/rate shown and source recorded.
Exact duplicate file (same SHA-256).
Likely duplicate transaction: same vendor/location, date, gallons and total within tolerance — evidence listed.
Receipt and fuel card row describe the same purchase (expected; merged as corroboration, not counted twice).
Vehicle has fuel purchases in the quarter but no mileage records.
Fuel purchased in a jurisdiction where the vehicle shows zero miles that quarter.
Fleet MPG outside the configured plausible band (TEMPORARY DEFAULT 4.0–9.0).
Odometer readings on receipts are not increasing over time for a vehicle, or conflict with ELD miles.
IFTA rate table for the quarter is not loaded.
Quarter has unresolved error-severity issues; worksheet must be labeled preliminary.
Fuel card purchase with no matching receipt.
Receipt paid by card with no matching card row (statement may be missing).
Document not attributable to a vehicle.

facts_to_respect: IFTA covers the 48 contiguous U.S. states and 10 Canadian provinces; returns are filed quarterly with the base jurisdiction.
Qualified motor vehicles: two axles and over 26,000 lb gross/registered weight, three or more axles, or a combination over 26,000 lb.
Records (distance and fuel) must be retained 4 years from the later of the due date or filing date.
calculation: total_miles = sum of all jurisdiction miles for qualified vehicles (taxable and non-taxable as reported).
total_taxable_gallons = sum of motor-fuel gallons purchased for qualified vehicles in the quarter (excluding reefer fuel and DEF).
fleet_mpg = total_miles / total_taxable_gallons (rounded per base-jurisdiction rules from config; default 2 decimals).
tax[j] = net_taxable_gallons[j] × rate[j] (+ surcharge[j] where the rate table defines one)
Rates come only from the official quarterly IFTA rate table loaded into ifta_rate_tables with source URL and import date; never from an LLM.
Use decimal arithmetic (no floats) and document every rounding step in the worksheet.
ifta_logic.labels: Worksheet header states PRELIMINARY until all error issues are resolved and the owner approves; REVIEWED after approval. Always include: 'Prepared for review by a qualified preparer; not a filed return.'

data_model.database: PostgreSQL. Every tenant-owned table has company_id and is protected by row-level security or an enforced query scope. Money stored as NUMERIC(12,2); gallons as NUMERIC(12,3).

period_pdf_report: Cover: company, USDOT/MC, period, generation date/time, status (PRELIMINARY/REVIEWED), snapshot id.
Summary: documents received, transactions, % verified, open issues by severity.
Fuel: gallons and dollars by state and fuel type; reefer and DEF shown separately.
Mileage and MPG by vehicle (when mileage imported).
Exceptions list with codes, explanations and links/page refs to source documents.
Reconciliation notes: formulas, included/excluded records, rounding.
Appendix: transaction table; optional supporting-document images.
Footer on every page: page x of y, company, period, status.
deliverables_spec.supporting_package: ZIP of original files renamed <date>_<state>_<vendor>_<transaction_id>.<ext> plus index.csv mapping files to transactions.
deliverables_spec.ifta_worksheet: Per-jurisdiction table: total miles, taxable miles, taxable gallons consumed, tax-paid gallons, net taxable gallons, rate, surcharge, tax due/credit; fleet totals and MPG; rate table source; PRELIMINARY/REVIEWED label.
deliverables_spec.audit_binder_phase2: Quarter archive with all of the above plus edit history and approvals, for an auditor.

web_application.platform: Responsive web application, designed for desktop and iPhone

initial_pages.Dashboard: Recent batches, processing status, pending reviews, summary metrics, and alerts.
initial_pages.Documents: Upload, search, filter, preview, and manage source files.
initial_pages.Transactions: Structured transaction ledger with source links, confidence, and edit history.
initial_pages.Audit Center: Duplicate candidates, missing fields, arithmetic issues, mismatches, and exceptions.
initial_pages.Reports: Generate, preview, and download PDF reports and CSV exports.
initial_pages.Company Settings: Manage company profiles, reporting preferences, trucks, users, and permissions.

design_principles: Built for a busy owner on a phone: large tap targets, one primary action per screen, plain words, no accounting jargon without explanation.
Every number is tappable and opens its source evidence.
Status colors are consistent everywhere: Verified (green), Needs Attention (amber), Unable to Verify (red/grey), with text labels for accessibility.
All UI strings externalized for i18n; English and Somali at launch; dates, money and numbers localized.
Loading, empty, success and error states on every screen.
WCAG 2.1 AA contrast and keyboard navigation on desktop.

notifications: Information needed (e.g. 'Which truck was this?') with one-tap or one-word reply.
Deadline reminders: 30, 14, 7 and 2 days before each IFTA due date.
Messages are sent in the user's language and channel; respect quiet hours.

operating_loop: Confirm selected company and reporting period.
Extract structured data with source references.
Validate the data and perform deterministic calculations.
Summarize verified findings and unresolved issues.
Ask for clarification when evidence is insufficient.
Generate a deliverable with clear scope, status, and limitations.
rules: Use structured JSON for extracted records.
Never fabricate values, citations, source references, or confidence scores.
Keep extracted source facts separate from calculated results.
Flag conflicting evidence rather than silently choosing a value.
Maintain an audit trail of edits, approvals, exports, and consequential actions.
Use deterministic code for arithmetic instead of relying on free-form language model calculations.
Do not submit filings, send payments, or take consequential external actions without explicit user authorization.
Never treat a model's self-review as verification; verification means rule checks, independent corroboration, or a human.
When asking a customer for information, ask one specific question at a time, in their language.
Never message a customer, driver or third party on the company's behalf except through the defined notification templates.

security_and_reliability: Use secure authentication and role-based permissions.
Isolate data by company and account.
Use appropriate encryption in transit and at rest.
Keep API keys and secrets out of browser code.
Avoid unnecessary logging of sensitive document content.
Define retention, export, and deletion policies.
Back up important records and test recovery.
Log who changed, approved, exported, or deleted records.
Use fictional demo data in public demos.
Do not claim certifications or regulatory compliance that have not been verified.
Retain IFTA-related documents and records at least 4 years from the later of the return due date or filing date; deletion requests for records under retention are queued with an explanation.
Serve documents only through short-lived signed URLs; no public buckets.
Encrypt sensitive identifiers (IFTA account numbers, EINs) at the field level.
Verify inbound webhook signatures (Twilio, email provider).
Rate-limit uploads and inbound messages per company and sender.
Enforce tenant isolation with automated tests that try cross-company access.
Daily database backups with a tested restore; object storage versioning on.
Plan for SOC 2 once selling to partners; do not claim it before it exists.

technical_architecture.approach: Build one complete vertical slice before adding all modules.
requirements: Keep ingestion, extraction, validation, calculations, reporting, and UI as separable components.
Prevent duplicate processing where possible through idempotent workflows.
Test rounding, duplicates, missing fields, and conflicting records.
Document local setup, environment variables, database migrations, and deployment.
Choose a maintainable technology stack based on cost, skills, security, and deployment requirements; explain trade-offs before committing.
Use decimal math libraries for money and gallons; never JavaScript floats.
Version every rule, prompt and rate table; store versions on the records they produced.
Make every deliverable reproducible from its snapshot id.
Startup preflight checks: verify each external credential (AI, storage, messaging, email) and fail loudly with a readable error.
Verify features on the deployed environment, not only locally; document which branch deploys where.

recommended_stack_TEMPORARY_DEFAULT.why: Matches a stack the founder already runs in production (TypeScript, Next.js, Express/Prisma, Postgres, Redis, Railway/Vercel), so it is cheap to operate and easy to maintain. Change only with a written trade-off.
recommended_stack_TEMPORARY_DEFAULT.frontend: Next.js (App Router) + TypeScript + Tailwind, installable PWA, i18n library (e.g. next-intl).
recommended_stack_TEMPORARY_DEFAULT.api: Node.js + TypeScript (Express or Next route handlers), Zod for validation.
recommended_stack_TEMPORARY_DEFAULT.database: PostgreSQL + Prisma; row-level company scoping enforced in a data-access layer and tested.
recommended_stack_TEMPORARY_DEFAULT.queue: Redis + BullMQ for extraction, matching and report jobs; idempotency keys per document/pass.
recommended_stack_TEMPORARY_DEFAULT.storage: S3-compatible object storage (e.g. Cloudflare R2 or S3) with versioning and signed URLs.
recommended_stack_TEMPORARY_DEFAULT.ai: Anthropic Claude vision models via server-side API for pass A; pass B via a second prompt/model or OCR + parse. Model IDs in env vars.
recommended_stack_TEMPORARY_DEFAULT.messaging: Twilio for SMS/WhatsApp; an inbound-email provider (e.g. Resend/Postmark inbound) for forwarding.
recommended_stack_TEMPORARY_DEFAULT.pdf: HTML templates rendered to PDF with Playwright/Chromium for consistent professional layout.
recommended_stack_TEMPORARY_DEFAULT.observability: Sentry for errors; structured logs without document contents.
recommended_stack_TEMPORARY_DEFAULT.hosting: Railway (API, workers, Postgres, Redis) + Vercel (web), or a single provider if simpler.

cost_controls: Log tokens and cost per extraction run; show cost per document and per company in an admin view.
Skip pass B for fields already corroborated by a fuel card row, when configured.
Downscale images to the smallest resolution that keeps accuracy on the test set.
Cache station-directory lookups; never re-extract an unchanged document (hash check).
Monthly AI budget cap per environment with alerts at 50/80/100%.

quality: Field accuracy vs golden set (target ≥ 98% on material fields)
Touchless rate: % receipts Verified with no human edit (target ≥ 70% at pilot end)
False-verified rate: Verified records later corrected (target < 0.5%)
speed: Median time from upload to Verified
Time from last document to period report

test_plan.golden_dataset: Create at least 60 fictional receipt images and PDFs with known correct answers: clean, faded thermal, crumpled, angled, multi-receipt photo, multi-page PDF, reefer + tractor fuel on one receipt, DEF, liters/CAD, missing unit number, duplicates, refunds/credits, and a matching fuel card CSV and ELD mileage CSV for a fictional 3-truck fleet quarter.
automated_tests: Every validation rule (pass and fail cases).
IFTA math with decimal rounding against hand-calculated fixtures.
Report regeneration from snapshot is byte-identical in data.
Extraction regression run against the golden set with an accuracy report on every prompt/model change.

acceptance_criteria: A user can upload multiple fuel receipts for one company and reporting period.
Every transaction links to its source document.
Missing and uncertain fields are flagged instead of invented.
Likely duplicate receipts are flagged with explanations.
State-by-state gallons are calculated from supported records only.
Fuel charges are separated from non-fuel charges and credits where supported.
PDF reports identify the company, reporting period, generation date, and review status.
Users can correct extracted data while preserving the original value and change history.
Users can download PDF and CSV deliverables.
The app works on desktop and mobile layouts.
Automated tests cover calculations, rounding, duplicate detection, missing data, and conflicting records.
A driver can send a receipt photo by SMS/WhatsApp or email and it appears in the company's inbox attributed to the right truck or is flagged S001.
A fuel card CSV can be imported with a saved mapping and matched to receipts without double-counting gallons.
An ELD mileage report can be imported and the IFTA worksheet computes fleet MPG and per-jurisdiction net gallons with decimal math matching hand-calculated fixtures.
Reefer fuel and DEF are never included in IFTA motor-fuel gallons.
Every material field shows both extraction passes and the final source.
The worksheet and report say PRELIMINARY while any error-severity issue is open.
Owner-facing screens and notifications are available in English and Somali.
Cross-company data access attempts fail in automated tests.
Documents cannot be hard-deleted inside their retention period.

definition_of_success: A trucking owner can upload a batch of receipts, get an organized and traceable transaction ledger, understand flagged problems, review the results, and export a professional report without manually organizing every receipt. A small-fleet owner sends paperwork from their phone, never types data, and receives a verified, audit-ready monthly report and a preparer-ready IFTA worksheet on time — with every number traceable to its source and nothing invented.
